title: Fuzzy clock overflows when on vertical panel
line: The Fuzzy Clock now wraps its text onto several lines in a vertical panel instead of spilling past the panel's edges.
explanation: In a vertical panel the Fuzzy Clock kept its text on one line (Text.NoWrap), and the visible label could not go below the normal label font size, so phrases like "Twenty past three" were wider than the panel and ran past both edges, clipped at the screen edge. The change wraps the text between words in vertical panels and lets the label shrink to the same minimum size the hidden size helper already uses, so the widget grows taller to fit the wrapped lines.

commits.message:
applets/fuzzy-clock: wrap the text in vertical panels

The time text never wrapped and could not shrink below the normal label
size, so longer phrases spilled past both edges of a vertical panel. It
now wraps between words there, using the size helper's minimum size.

BUG: 479714

patches.diff:
From 1df002fed32251360b949593e4a74af683a02082 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 03:19:25 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] applets/fuzzy-clock: wrap the text in vertical panels

The time text never wrapped and could not shrink below the normal label
size, so longer phrases spilled past both edges of a vertical panel. It
now wraps between words there, using the size helper's minimum size.

BUG: 479714
---
 applets/fuzzy-clock/qml/FuzzyClock.qml | 6 +++---
 1 file changed, 3 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)

diff --git a/applets/fuzzy-clock/qml/FuzzyClock.qml b/applets/fuzzy-clock/qml/FuzzyClock.qml
index e9f59c32b..330da15d5 100644
--- a/applets/fuzzy-clock/qml/FuzzyClock.qml
+++ b/applets/fuzzy-clock/qml/FuzzyClock.qml
@@ -266,11 +266,11 @@ Item {
             italic: Plasmoid.configuration.italicText
             pixelSize: 1024
         }
-        minimumPixelSize: Kirigami.Units.iconSizes.sizeForLabels
+        minimumPixelSize: main.vertical ? sizehelper.minimumPixelSize : Kirigami.Units.iconSizes.sizeForLabels
         fontSizeMode: Text.Fit
         text: main.timeString()
 
-        wrapMode: Text.NoWrap
+        wrapMode: main.vertical ? Text.WordWrap : Text.NoWrap
         horizontalAlignment: Text.AlignHCenter
         verticalAlignment: Text.AlignVCenter
         height: 0
@@ -301,7 +301,7 @@ Item {
         text: timeLabel.text
         fontSizeMode: main.vertical ? Text.HorizontalFit : Text.VerticalFit
 
-        wrapMode: Text.NoWrap
+        wrapMode: main.vertical ? Text.WordWrap : Text.NoWrap
         visible: false
         anchors {
             fill: parent
--

review.text: Clean, minimal fix in FuzzyClock.qml that enables word-boundary wrapping (Text.WordWrap) on both timeLabel and sizehelper in vertical panels and lowers timeLabel.minimumPixelSize to match sizehelper.minimumPixelSize. Using Text.WordWrap rather than Text.Wrap is the right choice here because sizehelper uses Text.HorizontalFit, where Text.Wrap would break words mid-word at a huge font size instead of shrinking. Horizontal panels and desktop placements are untouched, there are no binding loops, and the screenshots and regression tests across 30/46/120 px panels verify the expected UX.

reviews.text: Clean, minimal fix in FuzzyClock.qml that enables word-boundary wrapping (Text.WordWrap) on both timeLabel and sizehelper in vertical panels and lowers timeLabel.minimumPixelSize to match sizehelper.minimumPixelSize. Using Text.WordWrap rather than Text.Wrap is the right choice here because sizehelper uses Text.HorizontalFit, where Text.Wrap would break words mid-word at a huge font size instead of shrinking. Horizontal panels and desktop placements are untouched, there are no binding loops, and the screenshots and regression tests across 30/46/120 px panels verify the expected UX.

Implements the wrapping Nate asked for in c3: in vertical panels both the visible label and the hidden size helper use WordWrap, so Layout.minimumHeight follows the wrapped height and the widget grows taller, and the label may shrink to the helper's minimum size instead of being stuck at sizeForLabels. The helper only fits horizontally, so its height feeding back into the layout does not create a binding loop, and horizontal panels are untouched. The before/after screenshots show text clipped at the screen edge vs. 'Twenty past three' wrapped inside a 46 px panel, and 30/120 px and horizontal panels were checked; commit message and line match the 3-line diff.
